init.help:
Usage: data-cap init

Scaffolds a minimal data-cap starting point into the current directory:

  <src>/data.ts            a starter capability (buildData + documentData)
  scripts/generate-data.mjs a script that generates the manifest + docs artifacts,
                           or with --check fails when they are stale

Never overwrites an existing file, never runs anything, never edits
package.json. Everything else (generating artifacts, adding getters/
mutators, reading the snapshot) is printed as a next step. Run generation
afterwards with `node scripts/generate-data.mjs`, and add `--check` in CI.

data-cap.help:
data-cap - generate a persisted Evidence Model from discovered capabilities

Usage:
  data-cap init
  data-cap --evidence <path> [options]

Examples:
  data-cap init                                         Scaffold a first data.ts and a generate script
  data-cap --evidence docs/data.evidence.json           Write the Evidence Model
  data-cap --evidence docs/data.evidence.json --check   Fail if it is out of date (for CI)

Commands:
  init                        Scaffold a minimal starting point (one data.ts + a generate script); run `data-cap init --help` for details

--evidence is required (for a non-init invocation).

Where to look:
  --root <path>               Directory to resolve globs from (default: cwd)
  --include <glob>            Discovery glob (repeatable, default: every .ts/.tsx file)
  --exclude <glob>            Glob to exclude from discovery (repeatable)
  --package <name>            Also discover a capability from an installed package's "dataCap.schema" field (repeatable)
  --tsconfig <path>           The tsconfig.json, relative to the root, whose paths and baseUrl resolve aliased imports
                              (default: tsconfig.json at root)
  --no-tsconfig               Do not resolve aliased imports

What to analyze:
  --flow-evidence             Trace each field through your functions, evaluate the flowPolicy rules your capabilities
                              declare, and add the result to the Evidence Model
  --observations <path>       Runtime observations from data-cap/observe, added to the Evidence Model and compared with
                              the static findings (a JSON array of events, or { "events": [...], "skips": [...] } to
                              also report what the recorder left out)

What to write:
  --evidence <path>           Write the Evidence Model as JSON at this path
  --expiring-within-days <n>  How many days out counts as "expiring soon" in the Lifecycle Model (default: 30)
  --json                      Print a machine-readable report instead of text
  --check                     Write nothing; exit 1 if the evidence is stale or missing

What counts as an error:
  --strict                    Treat every warning as an error (info is never one)
  --strict-docs               Treat static warnings as errors: ownership, sensitivity, duplication
  --strict-ownership          Treat proven usage warnings as errors: abandoned capabilities, unconsumed owned fields
  --rules <path>              A JSON file of rules enforced over the evidence (for example noPolicyViolations, maxUnknowns,
                              requireVerified); exit 1 if any is violated, and a rule whose analysis did not run is a violation
  --strict-flow               Treat data-flow warnings as errors: a sensitive field crossing a boundary, flow policies that
                              could not be decided, fields sent to a client whole or never used (with --flow-evidence)

  --help, -h                  Show the help text

The manifest, documentation catalog, ownership report and data-flow diagram are not generated by this CLI. Call
`generateManifest`, `generateDocumentation`, `generateUsage` and `generateFlow` (or `generateDataArtifacts`
and `checkArtifacts`) from `data-cap/build` in your own build script. A worked example:
https://github.com/MaverickCER/data-cap/tree/main/examples/application/scripts/generate-docs
Every flag is described in https://github.com/MaverickCER/data-cap/blob/main/GUIDE.md

## Sensitive data crossing an external boundary

BlastRadiusEntry.description: One changed capability's known current consumers.

capability.description: The capability key (`file#exportName`): matches `ManifestChangeReport`'s own key convention.

consumers.description: Distinct consuming files known (from Dependency Model) to depend on this capability right now, sorted.

CapabilityInventory.description: The one authoritative model every report generator reads from: see `buildInventory`. This type IS `data-cap`'s Capability Model (ADR 0050), not a separate thing that produces one: `CAPABILITY_MODEL_SCHEMA_VERSION` above versions this exact interface. ADR 0050 kept the `CapabilityInventory` and `buildInventory` names rather than add a `CapabilityModel` wrapper. This type was already the public model, so a rename would only duplicate it. A canonical, versioned, JSON-serializable projection of every discovered capability's fields and operations, active or not.

warnings.description: Parse/link warnings carried through from the discovery/linking pass that produced this inventory, each `file` root-relative like every other path this model publishes.

CapabilityNode.description: One `buildData`/`createData` capability, resolved from the inventory's shared model.

declarationPosition.description: Position of this capability's own `buildData`/`createData` call site: always available (ADR 0052).

docs.description: This capability's own declared documentation, if any. It is the single path for `owner`, `sensitivity`, `purpose`, `legalBasis`, `dataResidency` and `auditRequired` (ADR 0057). A capability has nothing above it to resolve against, so a separate "resolved" property would only copy `docs.X`.

exportName.description: The binding name the `buildData`/`createData` result is exported as.

file.description: Root-relative POSIX path of the file declaring this capability: the one place an absolute discovery path is converted for publication (see `display-path.ts`). Every downstream model that carries a capability's `file` (Ownership, Finding, Dependency, Manifest Snapshot) copies this value rather than re-deriving it, so there is exactly one conversion point. Re-derive a real path with `absolutePathFrom(root, file)` when actual filesystem/import work needs one.

kind.description: `"buildData"` or `"createData"`: which call form declared this capability.

ChangeModel.description: `data-cap`'s Change Model: the manifest diff, plus an optional blast-radius index.

blastRadius.description: One entry per added/updated capability, or `undefined` when no `DependencyModel` was supplied: an optional layer, matching `--ownership`/`--flow`'s existing opt-in cost model (the usage scan isn't free).

renamedFields.description: Every added-field/removed-field pair this run's currently-declared `renamedFrom` values correlate into a single rename, sorted by capability key then current name.

hash.description: Whole-file SHA-256 (hex) of the cited file's content, at the moment this citation was last confirmed to exist. An integrity signal only ("this file hasn't visibly changed since the citation was written") never proof the citation's own underlying claim is semantically correct (see ADR 0053).

derivedFrom.description: Which sub-models this claim was derived from.

lastObservedAt.description: The latest time any backing observation was seen (ISO 8601, UTC); absent when none carried a time.

observedPaths.description: The capability-qualified names of the observed paths that back this claim, sorted and distinct; absent when none did.

pathCoverage.description: Whether those paths cover the claim's whole path scope; present exactly when `observedPaths` is.

statement.description: Human-readable statement, derived from the structured fields and never parsed.

status.description: Epistemic status of the underlying fact: the weakest status along the static path, or `observed` for an observation-only claim.

ClaimPathCoverage.description: Whether the observations seen cover the claim's whole path scope or only narrower paths inside it.

ClaimScope.description: What a claim covers and how completely.

observationScopes.description: Every observation scope that contributed to the claim, sorted; empty when none were run or none matched.

traceComplete.description: False when the static trace behind the claim touched an `unknown` fact: the real picture may be larger.

truncatedScopes.description: Contributing observation scopes whose recorder reported leaving out evidence near this claim's field, sorted; absent when none.

ClaimVerification.description: How the evidence lines up for a claim.

DataFlowDirection.description: Which direction data moves across a declared boundary, and what kind of boundary it is. Author-declared documentation only: never statically verified against an operation's actual `execute`/`subscribe` body (those stay opaque per `AGENTS.md` invariant 6). A report may never present an endpoint as a proven fact; see `AGENTS.md`'s declared-vs-proven invariant.

DataFlowEndpoint.description: One declared data-flow boundary an operation crosses. A getter's or subscription's endpoints are typically `"input"`: where `execute` or `subscribe` acquires data from. A mutator's are typically `"output"`: where it sends data to. Nothing enforces the typical case, since this is documentation, not a runtime contract.

direction.description: Which way data moves across this boundary.

handling.description: The declared data-safety state of this field's value AT this specific boundary crossing. For example, a field can arrive `"encrypted"` on an `"input"` endpoint and leave `"redacted"` on an `"output"` endpoint. Declared only, like every other field in this vocabulary. It records what a developer states about handling at this crossing, never that data-cap verified the runtime value matches it.

kind.description: What kind of boundary this is.

name.description: Short identifier, e.g. "stripe-api", "postgres:users"; a semantic label, not a sentence.

url.description: A literal, trackable location for this endpoint: a URL, a route path, a `table:column` reference. Unlike `name` (a short label), it is compared and matched across capabilities, not only read by a person. For example, two capabilities that declare the same URL are flagged as likely duplicate fetches.

DataFlowEndpointKind.description: What kind of boundary a declared data-flow endpoint crosses: a data store (`database`/`cache`/`storage`/`queue`), an external entity (`api`/`external-service`/`user-input`), or something internal to this codebase (`computed`/`internal`).

DependencyEdge.description: A statically-proven connection from one consuming file to a capability (or a specific field/operation on it). Unlike the declared metadata in `core/document.ts` (`source`, `credentials`, `endpoints`), every `DependencyEdge` is derived by AST analysis, never author-declared: see `AGENTS.md`'s declared-vs-proven invariant. Produced by the usage-scan pass (`scan-dependencies.ts`), not by this module.

from.description: The consuming file, as a root-relative POSIX path (see `display-path.ts`).

position.description: Position of the access site in `from` (file already known via `from`). Set when this edge originates from a specific identifier reference. That is every relationship except the file-level `"imports"` fallback edge scan-dependencies.ts synthesizes for a consumer with no further resolved usage.

relationship.description: Which kind of connection this is: see `DependencyRelationship`.

resolution.description: Whether the consumer reference itself was unambiguously resolved: see the usage-scan pass for what each value means.

capability.description: The capability being consumed.

exportName.description: The binding name the capability is exported as.

file.description: Root-relative POSIX path of the file declaring the capability: the same value `CapabilityNode.file` publishes.

field.description: The specific field path being read, when `relationship` is `"reads-field"`.

operation.description: The specific operation name being called, when `relationship` is `"calls-getter"`/`"calls-mutator"`/`"calls-subscription"`.

DependencyModel.description: `data-cap`'s Dependency Model: every proven `DependencyEdge`, unindexed. See `dependency-projections.ts` for on-demand capability/consumer groupings.

edges.description: Every proven edge, unindexed: same array `scanDependencies` produced.

DependencyRelationship.description: How a consuming file uses a capability: an import alone, a field read, or a call to a getter, mutator or subscription.

EvidenceComputedModels.description:
Which project-varying sub-models this particular run actually computed.

Without this, a persisted `data.evidence.json` is ambiguous in exactly the way a governance artifact must never be. An absent `dependency` could mean "nothing in this project depends on anything" (a real, reportable finding) or "this run never scanned for dependencies" (no finding at all, only an un-run pass). Those are opposite conclusions and the JSON looked identical either way.

env-cap solves the same ambiguity by always computing all six sub-models, so absence never happens. `data-cap` deliberately does not follow that: the usage scan is the expensive pass here, and `--docs` alone is supposed to stay cheap. So instead of forcing every run to pay for a full dependency scan, each sub-model's presence is stated explicitly.

`capability`, `lifecycle`, and `runtimeContract` have no flag: they are always populated by construction, so a flag could only ever read `true`.

A pass that ran and found nothing is `true` with an empty result, never `false`. "We looked and found none" is a real finding, and this field keeps it apart from "we did not look".

change.description: Whether a manifest diff was available and produced a Change Model this run.

claims.description: Whether claims were derived this run: true exactly when `flow` was computed.

dependency.description: Whether a usage scan ran and produced a Dependency Model this run.

finding.description: Whether at least one rule/scan pass ran and produced a Finding Model this run.

flow.description: Whether a flow pass ran and produced a Flow Model this run.

observation.description: Whether runtime observations were ingested and produced an Observation Model this run.

ownership.description: Whether an Ownership Model was built this run.

policy.description: Whether policy rules were evaluated and produced a Policy Model this run.

EvidenceModel.description: `data-cap`'s Evidence Model: the composition of Capability, Lifecycle, Dependency, Ownership, Finding, Change, and Runtime Contract Model into one provenance-stamped artifact.

capability.description: Capability Model.

change.description: Change Model, or `undefined` when no manifest diff was available. See `computed.change` before reading absence as "nothing changed." It is not a diffable input across two `EvidenceModel`s the way the other five project-varying fields conceptually are: it already IS a diff.

claims.description: Claims Model, derived by `buildEvidenceModel` from `flow` (plus `policy` and `observation` when present), never supplied by a caller. There is one derivation path, so the claims can never disagree with the facts they cite. `undefined` exactly when `flow` is.

computed.description: Which of the four optional sub-models below this run actually computed: read this before concluding anything from an absent one.

dependency.description: Dependency Model, or `undefined` when no usage scan was run: see `computed.dependency` before reading absence as "no dependencies."

finding.description: Finding Model, or `undefined` when nothing was supplied. See `computed.finding` before reading absence as "no findings."

flow.description: Flow Model, or `undefined` when no flow pass ran: see `computed.flow` before reading absence as "no flows."

lifecycle.description: Lifecycle Model: always populated, for the reason `EvidenceModelInputs.lifecycle` documents.

observation.description: Observation Model, or `undefined` when no observations were ingested. See `computed.observation` before reading absence as "nothing was observed."

ownership.description: Ownership Model, or `undefined` when none was supplied: see `computed.ownership`.

policy.description: Policy Model, or `undefined` when no rules were evaluated: see `computed.policy`.

provenance.description: Who/when/what produced this instance: always present (see `EvidenceProvenance`).

runtimeContract.description: Runtime Contract Model: always populated, package-scoped rather than project-scoped (see this module's own doc comment). A static append, never itself a diffable "changed since last run" input.

EvidenceProvenance.description:
Who/when/what produced a given `EvidenceModel` instance: matching env-cap's own `EvidenceProvenance` shape exactly, so a consumer reading both packages' evidence artifacts reads one vocabulary, not two.

`generatedAt`/`toolVersion` are required: every real caller can supply both. (The tool version is `data-cap`'s own installed version, read from its `package.json`; see `package-version.ts`.) A provenance stamp that might be missing either one is a provenance stamp no consumer can rely on. `commit` stays caller-supplied and explicitly `string | undefined` (never omitted from the shape). `data-cap` never shells out to `git` itself, so an absent commit is a stated absence, never a guess. This is ADR 0050's "provenance is caller-supplied, never ambient-detected" convention, kept exactly where it still applies.

commit.description: The commit SHA this evidence was generated against, or `undefined` when the caller didn't supply one.

generatedAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp for when this evidence was generated.

toolVersion.description: `data-cap`'s own installed version at generation time.

EvidenceRef.description: A pointer to one record inside the Evidence Model.

id.description: Flow node/edge id, observation id, or `ruleId#fieldNodeId` for a policy result group.

EvidenceRefModel.description: Which sub-model of the Evidence Model a piece of evidence lives in.

evaluated.description: The rules that were evaluated, in order.

ok.description: True exactly when there are no violations.

EvidenceRuleViolation.description: One reason the gate did not pass.

evidence.description: The records in the evidence this rests on, for drill-down.

ExpiringEntry.description: One capability- or field-level `expiresAt` falling within the configured window (or already past it).

daysRemaining.description: Whole days from `now` until expiry; negative when already expired.

expiresAt.description: The raw ISO-8601 date string, exactly as declared.

exportName.description: The binding name the capability is exported as.

field.description: `undefined` for a capability-level `expiresAt`, set for a per-field one.

file.description: Root-relative POSIX path of the declaring file.

FieldDocs.description:
Documentation metadata for one field.

`owner`, `sensitivity`, `protections`, and `transferSafeguard` override the capability-level value of the same name for this field. Fields in one capability can differ in sensitivity, owner and transfer boundary. `protections` and `retention` only signal that documentation is present. A generator may say a safeguard or policy is "documented" or "not documented", never that it is adequate, correct or enforced. `purpose`, `legalBasis`, `dataResidency`, `transferSafeguard` and `auditRequired` follow the same presence-only rule. They are declared governance facts, never a claim that data-cap has determined they satisfy any law (see `specs/decisions/0051-documentdata-metadata-and-governance-fields.md`). `dataSubjectCategory` and `recipientCategories` are field-level only, with no capability-level counterpart; each property's own doc comment says why.

The boundary this interface draws is deliberate: a named property here is reserved for a concept data-cap itself understands, projects, or reports on. Anything else (organization-specific detail with no data-cap-defined meaning) belongs in `metadata`, never in an ad hoc extra property. That keeps this vocabulary bounded instead of accreting one-off keys over time.

Note what is deliberately absent: there is no per-field `validate`/ `validator` property, and no `helpers.validators` combinator library backing one, unlike `@maverickcer/env-cap`'s `EnvVarDocs`. That is a design choice, not a gap. `env-cap` validates on a reject-and-throw pipeline, where a failing validator must carry a message explaining the rejection. `data-cap` has no reject path to write a message for. Invalid processor/operation output resets the field to its declared default via `core/schema.ts`'s `checkValueAgainstSchema`. That keeps fields synchronously readable (`AGENTS.md` invariant 2) and surfaces the mismatch through `DataInfo`. See `helpers/shape.ts`'s own module comment for the full reasoning.

auditRequired.description: Whether access to this field is documented as requiring an audit trail. Declared only, same presence-only discipline as `protections`/ `retention`. Overrides the capability's own `auditRequired` for this field specifically.

dataResidency.description: The declared jurisdiction(s) this field's data is permitted or expected to be *stored* in. It is a policy constraint, not an observed fact, a processing-location claim or a data-subject-location claim. Overrides the capability's own `dataResidency` for this field specifically.

dataSubjectCategory.description: The declared category of data subject this field's data concerns (e.g. `"customers"`, `"employees"`, `"minors"`). Declared only: data-cap never verifies who a field's actual data subjects are. Field-level only, with no capability-level counterpart to override. Which data subjects a field concerns is a fact about that field's own data, not one a capability can state for every field.

deprecated.description: Whether this field is documented as deprecated. Presence-only, same discipline as every other declared fact here: nothing warns at runtime.

deprecatedReason.description: Why this field is deprecated, and what to use instead. Only meaningful alongside `deprecated`.

description.description: Why this field exists / what it's for.

expiresAt.description: When this field's data (or the credential/source behind it) is declared to stop being valid, as an ISO-8601 date (`"2026-12-31"`). Declared only: nothing expires anything at runtime, and `data-cap` never fetches a real expiry from a provider. Build tooling reads it to report what is expiring soon (see the Lifecycle Model). A date that has already passed is reported as expired, never acted on.

legalBasis.description: The declared legal basis asserted for processing this field (e.g. `"consent"`, `"contract"`, `"legitimate interest"`). Records that a basis was declared: never that data-cap has determined the basis is legally valid. Overrides the capability's own `legalBasis` for this field specifically.

metadata.description: Free-form extension bag for anything data-cap itself has no named concept for: opaque, never inspected or validated by any code path in this package. Once a concept matters enough for data-cap to reason about, it gets its own named field above; everything else stays here.

owner.description: Overrides the capability's own `owner` for this field specifically.

protections.description: Overrides the capability's own `protections` for this field specifically.

purpose.description: The declared reason this field's data is collected/retained. Declared only: data-cap never verifies the stated purpose matches actual usage. Overrides the capability's own `purpose` for this field specifically.

recipientCategories.description: The declared categories of recipient this field's data has been or will be disclosed to (e.g. `"payment processor"`, `"tax authority"`, `"internal support staff"`). Always explicitly authored: data-cap never infers a recipient category from its own dependency graph. A proven *consumer* inside this codebase is a different fact from a declared *external recipient*, and conflating them would misrepresent both. Field-level only, for the same reason as `dataSubjectCategory`. See `specs/decisions/0067-ropa-fields-recipient-categories-never-inferred.md` for the full reasoning on why this is never derived.

removeBy.description: The date by which a deprecated field is intended to be removed, ISO-8601. Field-level only: a removal deadline is about one field's own migration. A capability-wide `removeBy` would say nothing about which of its fields still need work.

renamedFrom.description: The previous name of this field, when it was renamed. Field-level only, for the same reason as `removeBy`. Build tooling uses it to read an added field and a removed field across two runs as one rename. Without it they are an unrelated addition and deletion (see `ChangeModel`'s `renamedFields`). Only ever populated from an *authored* value, never guessed from name similarity.

retention.description: Documented retention policy for this field: presence only, never an enforcement claim.

sensitivity.description: Overrides the capability's own `sensitivity` for this field specifically.

transferSafeguard.description: The declared safeguard relied on for any transfer of this field's data out of `dataResidency`'s jurisdictions, such as `"EU Standard Contractual Clauses"` or `"adequacy decision"`. `dataResidency` states where data may be *stored*; this states what protects a transfer *out of* that jurisdiction. Declared only: data-cap never verifies a transfer actually occurred or that the named safeguard is legally adequate. Overrides the capability's own `transferSafeguard` for this field specifically. See `specs/decisions/0067-ropa-fields-recipient-categories-never-inferred.md`.

FieldNode.description: One top-level field of a capability, resolved from the inventory's shared model.

auditRequired.description: Resolved: the field's own `docs.auditRequired`, else the capability's `auditRequired`; same inheritance rule (ADR 0051, ADR 0057).

dataResidency.description: Resolved: the field's own `docs.dataResidency`, else the capability's `dataResidency`; same inheritance rule. The declared permitted-storage jurisdiction(s), not an observed fact (ADR 0051, ADR 0057).

declarationPosition.description: Position of this field's own key in the `fields` object literal. Set only when `fields` was resolved as an inline literal in this file. It is `undefined` when identifier-resolved across a file boundary this pass doesn't retain AST access to (never guessed at; ADR 0052).

docs.description: This field's own declared documentation, if any: `description`/`protections`/`retention`/`metadata` have no resolution concept and live only here; for the six governed properties below, prefer `.value`/`.declaredOn` over reading this object directly (ADR 0057).

legalBasis.description: Resolved: the field's own `docs.legalBasis`, else the capability's `legalBasis`; same inheritance rule. A declared fact, never a legal determination (ADR 0051, ADR 0057).

owner.description: Resolved: the field's own `docs.owner`, else the capability's `owner`, plus which one declared it.

path.description: Top-level field key, as a single-element path (see the module doc comment on why granularity stops here).

purpose.description: Resolved: the field's own `docs.purpose`, else the capability's `purpose`; same inheritance rule as `owner`/`sensitivity` (ADR 0051, ADR 0057). Declared only, never verified.

sensitivity.description: Resolved: the field's own `docs.sensitivity`, else the capability's `sensitivity`; same inheritance rule as `owner` (ADR 0049, ADR 0050, ADR 0057).

shape.description: The field's literal-evaluated declared default: structural comparison only (e.g. `structural-duplication.ts`), never a runtime value.

writtenBy.description: Every getter/mutator/subscription whose statically-extracted `writes` shape claims this field.

kind.description: Which kind of operation wrote this field.

indeterminateSites.description: Every candidate access site a `"FIELD_ACCESS_INDETERMINATE"` finding could actually be about (ADR 0052): populated only for that code. Lives here, on the one variant that can carry it, rather than as a flat sibling of `location`: a field-level finding is the only kind that ever has one. Spans potentially multiple consuming files, so each entry carries its own `file` (`SourceLocation`, not only `SourcePosition`).

FindingLocation.description: Where a finding points, as a discriminated union: never a formatted string a consumer would have to parse back apart. Ships with only the variants `findings.ts`'s actual emission sites produce today (`"capability"`/`"field"`/`"consumer"`/`"none"`). `"operation"` is included because `ReportFinding.operation` is already part of that type's public shape, even though no current finding populates it. It is trivially reachable the day one does, not a guess about what it would look like. `"capability"`, `"field"` and `"operation"` carry an optional `position` (ADR 0052): the declaration site, when the source `ReportFinding.position` was set. `"consumer"` has none, since a *consuming file* has no single declaration position.

FindingLocationCapability.description: A finding's capability locator: shared by every `FindingLocation` variant except `"none"`.

exportName.description: The binding name the capability is exported as.

file.description: Root-relative POSIX path of the file declaring the capability: carried through verbatim from `CapabilityNode.file` (see `display-path.ts`).

FindingModel.description: `data-cap`'s Finding Model: every finding, with a structured, pre-computed `location`.

findings.description: Every finding, each with its `location` computed.

FlowBoundaryKind.description: What a data-flow rule can name as a destination: the declared endpoint kinds, plus the two destinations only code analysis can see.

FlowCoverage.description: What was and was not analyzed: a projection must not call a graph complete unless `complete`.

complete.description: True only when nothing above is non-zero apart from `functionsAnalyzed`.

functionsAnalyzed.description: Function nodes whose status is not `unknown`.

FlowEdge.description: One edge of the Flow Model.

handling.description: The data-safety state of the value at this hop, when declared or established: policy evaluation reads it at boundary crossings.

origin.description: Id of the `field` node whose data this edge carries. Present on every data-carrying edge the flow pass derives, so a helper shared by several fields does not make each field appear to reach every other field's destinations. Absent on edges that are not about one field's data (a `calls` edge). `path` is expressed in the origin field's frame.

path.description: The field path this edge carries, for a field-sensitive edge; absent for an edge about the whole value or about control.

source.description: Where in source this edge arises (a call site, a read), when known.

FlowEdgeKind.description: What an edge means. Data moves `from` -> `to` along `reads`, `writes`, `transforms`, `passes`, `returns` and `crosses-boundary`. `calls` is control flow, and `discards` records that a function received a field and did not forward it. Neither carries data, so tracing does not follow them. `side-effect` links a function to the boundary it acts on.

FlowEdgeTag.description: One tag of the Flow Model.

edge.description: Id of the existing edge that carries the data at this place (an edge id as `flowEdgeId` derives it).

fresh.description: With `copy`: the value copied was already a fresh copy.

source.description: Where the copy, the derivation or the hand-over is.

unused.description: With `derive`: nothing ever reads the derived value.

FlowHandling.description: The declared data-safety state of a value at a boundary crossing: the vocabulary of `DataFlowEndpoint.handling` and of flow policy rules.

coverage.description: What was and was not analyzed.

edgeTags.description: What the scanner saw happen to the data of some edges, ordered by id. Absent when it saw nothing worth noting (ADR 0075).

unknowns.description: Every explicit unknown, ordered by id.

FlowNode.description: One node of the Flow Model.

boundaryKind.description: What kind of boundary this is; only meaningful (and required by policy evaluation) on a `boundary` node.

classification.description: Declared or inherited sensitivity classification, when known: carried verbatim, never inferred here.

scope.description: Root-relative POSIX path of the file that declares this node, or a stable namespace for a node with no file (a boundary).

source.description: Declaration position within `scope`, when there is one.

FlowPolicyAppliesTo.description: Which fields a rule applies to; every supplied criterion must match, and at least one is required.

classification.description: Exact match against a field node's `classification`.

field.description: Exact match against a field node's `name` (for example `User.email`).

path.description: Narrows the rule to one path inside each matching field (for example `["passwordHash"]`): only flow of that path, or of the whole field, counts.

scope.description: Restricts the rule to fields declared in this file (a root-relative path); never sufficient on its own.

FlowPolicyAppliesToDocs.description: Which fields a data-flow rule governs; every supplied criterion must match, and `classification` or `field` is required.

classification.description: Every field of this capability whose resolved `sensitivity` equals this value.

field.description: One field of this capability, by its top-level key.

path.description: Narrows the rule to one path inside each governed field (for example `["passwordHash"]`).

FlowPolicyDocs.description: One declared data-flow rule: which of this capability's fields it governs, and what must hold wherever their data goes. Evaluated against the Flow Model at build time. A rule is a declaration, never a runtime check. A result is only as complete as the analysis behind it (see the Policy Model's `indeterminate` outcome). At least one of `forbidDestinations`, `allowedDestinations` and `requireHandling` is required.

allowedDestinations.description: If set, the only destinations the governed data may reach.

allowedHandling.description: Handling that exempts a crossing from `forbidDestinations`/`allowedDestinations`.

forbidDestinations.description: Destinations the governed data must never reach.

requireHandling.description: If set, every crossing of the governed data must declare one of these handlings.

FlowPolicyRule.description: One declared data-flow rule. At least one constraint must be set.

allowedDestinations.description: If set, the only boundary kinds the governed fields may reach.

allowedHandling.description: Handling that exempts a crossing from `forbidDestinations`/`allowedDestinations`.

forbidDestinations.description: Boundary kinds the governed fields must never reach.

requireHandling.description: If set, every boundary crossing of a governed field must declare one of these handlings.

FlowStatus.description: ADR 0071: the five epistemic statuses, shared by every flow fact, claim and finding.

FlowUnknown.description: An explicit record that part of the program could not be analyzed.

data.description: The tracked data that entered the part of the program that could not be followed. Absent means "unknown which data": every trace that reaches the subject must treat itself as incomplete. Present, it lets a trace of a different field or an unrelated path stay complete: an opaque call that only ever saw `email` says nothing about where `passwordHash` went.

items.description: A piece of capability-field data an unknown concerns: the field node and the path inside it.

origin.description: Id of the `field` node the data comes from.

path.description: Path inside the field; `[]` is the whole field.

source.description: Where the unanalyzable construct is.

subject.description: The node this unknown prevents us from fully describing, when there is one.

FlowUnknownReason.description: Why a part of the program could not be analyzed (ADR 0053 citations apply to each).

FlowVia.description:
What the scanner saw happen to the data of an edge at one place, beyond what the edge says (ADR 0075).

- `serialize-roundtrip`: the data was taken apart and put back together with nothing in between that reads it (`JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(x))`, `Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(x))`).
- `copy`: the data was copied and nothing was added, dropped or renamed (`structuredClone(x)`, `{...x }`, `[...x]`, `Array.from(x)`). `fresh` says the copied value was itself a copy made by one of these.
- `derive`: a value computed from the data was bound to a name that is never read (`unused`).
- `forward`: reserved for a producer that knows a function only hands the data on. The scanner does not emit it; forwarding chains are found from the edges alone, so no reader depends on this tag.

GenerateDocumentationResult.description: The rendered documentation catalog plus the ownership/sensitivity findings it surfaces.

location.description: Where this documentation is intended to be written.

GenerateFlowFile.description: One file within the generated flow artifact set.

path.description: Absolute output path.

GenerateFlowResult.description: The generated Data Flow Diagram + Security Data-Flow Review set.

files.description: Every generated file in the set.

findings.description: This pass's own findings only (`SENSITIVE_DATA_CROSSES_EXTERNAL_BOUNDARY`): `additionalFindings` are folded into the rendered review but not echoed back here, so a caller aggregating findings across every generator never double-counts them.

location.description: The directory this set was written under.

GenerateManifestResult.description: The rendered manifest plus everything needed to persist and diff it against a future run.

changes.description: The diff against `previousSnapshot`, or an all-added report on a first run.

location.description: Where this manifest is intended to be written.

snapshot.description: The current inventory's snapshot: persist this to enable "changes since last report" on the next run.

GenerateUsageResult.description: The rendered Dependency & Ownership report plus the proven `DependencyEdge`s and findings it's built from.

edges.description: Every proven consumer relationship the scan found.

location.description: Where this report is intended to be written, or `undefined` when the caller requested only the scan results: see `GenerateUsageOptions.location`.

warnings.description: Parse/resolution warnings from the scan, never blocking.

JsonErrorInfo.description: A thrown error's shape in the `--json` envelope.

findings.description: Populated only when the thrown error carries a `ReportFinding[]` (`DataProjectGenerationError` always does).

JsonErrorPayload.description: The `--json` envelope for a failed run (generation threw).

JsonReportPayload.description: The complete `--json` envelope shape, success or failure: the target type the published JSON Schema (`schemas/data-cap-report.schema.json`, `npm run schema`) is generated from.

JsonSuccessPayload.description: The `--json` envelope for a successful run (generation completed without throwing).

checkResult.description: Present only when invoked with --check. Governs --check's own pass/fail exit code, independent of this envelope's top-level `ok` (which keeps its existing, unrelated meaning: "did generation complete without throwing").

evidence.description: `data-cap`'s Evidence Model (ADR 0050), composed from this same run's `inventory`/`usage`/`manifest`/`findings`: always present, unlike `manifest`/`documentation`/`usage`/`flow` above, since composing it costs nothing beyond data already held in memory. `--evidence` only controls whether it is *also written to disk*. Every consumer of `ReportResult`, `--json` included, gets the composed model on every run.

evidenceRules.description: Present only when invoked with --rules: the verdict of the rules enforced over this run's evidence.

findings.description: Every finding across every requested generator, after `--strict*` escalation.

hasBlockingErrors.description: True when `errorCount > 0`: `generateDataArtifacts` throws instead of writing when this is true.

usage.description: Always present: the usage scan runs on every call, whatever the flags. It yields proven consumption positions, dependency edges and ownership findings, which the Dependency Model needs. `--ownership` only controls whether the rendered report additionally gets *written to disk* (`usage.location`): `usage` itself, and its `edges`/`findings`, are always real.

warnings.description: Parse/link warnings from discovery, never blocking.

LifecycleModel.description: `data-cap`'s Lifecycle Model: declared expiry/deprecation/rename data, plus the expiring-soon view.

capabilities.description: Only capabilities with at least one lifecycle-relevant field set, at the capability level or on at least one field. Sorted by `file` then `exportName`.

expiring.description: Every capability-/field-level `expiresAt` within the configured window, soonest-first (already-expired entries sort first, since their `daysRemaining` is negative).

LifecycleModelCapability.description: One capability's declared lifecycle data, plus every lifecycle-bearing field under it.

deprecated.description: Whether the capability is documented as deprecated.

deprecatedReason.description: Why it's deprecated, when stated.

expiresAt.description: Declared ISO-8601 expiry for the capability as a whole.

exportName.description: The binding name the capability is exported as.

fields.description: Only fields with at least one lifecycle field set, sorted by path: same "only what's relevant" scope the rendered report uses.

file.description: Root-relative POSIX path: carried through verbatim from `CapabilityNode.file`.

retention.description: Declared retention policy at the capability level.

LifecycleModelField.description: One field's declared lifecycle data. Only fields with at least one of these set appear in the model at all.

deprecated.description: Whether the field is documented as deprecated.

deprecatedReason.description: Why it's deprecated, when stated.

expiresAt.description: Declared ISO-8601 expiry, unparsed and uninterpreted here.

path.description: The field's path within its capability: `readonly string[]`, matching every other model's field addressing (never a flat key string).

removeBy.description: Declared ISO-8601 removal deadline: field-level only (see `core/document.ts`).

renamedFrom.description: The field's previous name, when authored: what `ChangeModel.renamedFields` correlates against.

retention.description: Declared retention policy: a policy statement, deliberately independent of `expiresAt`'s temporal constraint (a field can be retained long after its source credential expires, and vice versa).

LocatedFinding.description: One finding, with its structured `location` computed, and *only* that. A rule/scan emits a `ReportFinding` carrying the raw, optional `capability`/`field`/`operation`/`source`/`position`/`indeterminateSites` locators (see `findings.ts`). `locationOf` resolves all six into one required, structured `location`, and this type then drops them. So a consumer has exactly one path to "where does this point". There is no structured answer sitting next to six flat ones that say the same thing (and could drift apart under a hand-constructed value). Two names for one lineage: emit a `ReportFinding`, consume a `LocatedFinding`.

code.description: Which kind of fact this finding reports.

evidence.description: The records in the Evidence Model this finding rests on: flow nodes and edges, a policy result, an unknown (ADR 0070). Lets a reader drill from the finding to the analysis behind it, and lets SARIF show the path. Absent for findings derived from declared metadata alone.

family.description: Which analysis pass produced this finding: see `ReportFindingFamily`.

severity.description: How strongly this finding should be treated.

active.description: Defaults to `true` when omitted. Gates `exclusiveGroup` conflict checks and manifest membership.

auditRequired.description: Whether access to this capability's data is documented as requiring an audit trail. Declared only, same presence-only discipline as `protections`/`retention`. A field's own `auditRequired` overrides this for that field specifically.

dataResidency.description: The declared jurisdiction(s) this capability's data is permitted or expected to be *stored* in. It is a policy constraint, not an observed fact, a processing-location claim or a data-subject-location claim. A field's own `dataResidency` overrides this for that field specifically.

deprecated.description: Whether this capability is documented as deprecated. Presence-only; nothing warns at runtime.

deprecatedReason.description: Why this capability is deprecated, and what to use instead. Only meaningful alongside `deprecated`.

description.description: Why this capability exists / what it's for.

exclusiveGroup.description: Mutual-exclusivity group: more than one *active* capability sharing this value is a real conflict (only one implementation of a group should be live at once).

expiresAt.description: When this capability's data (or the credential/source behind it) is declared to stop being valid, as an ISO-8601 date. A field's own `expiresAt` (see `FieldDocs`) overrides this for that field specifically. Declared only: nothing expires at runtime.

flowPolicy.description: Declared data-flow rules for this capability's fields, evaluated against the Flow Model (see `FlowPolicyDocs`).

legalBasis.description: The declared legal basis asserted for processing this capability's data (e.g. `"consent"`, `"contract"`, `"legitimate interest"`). Records that a basis was declared, never that data-cap has determined the basis is legally valid. It records declared governance facts; data-cap does not determine whether those facts satisfy a law. A field's own `legalBasis` overrides this for that field specifically.

metadata.description: Free-form extension bag for anything data-cap itself has no named concept for. It is opaque: no code path in this package inspects or validates it. An example is a jurisdiction-specific regulatory classification such as `{ regulatory: "GDPR,PCI-DSS" }`. Once a concept matters enough for data-cap to reason about, it gets its own named field above, as `purpose`, `legalBasis`, `dataResidency`, `transferSafeguard` and `auditRequired` did. Everything else stays here.

name.description: Display name: falls back to the export/binding name when omitted.

owner.description: Who's accountable for this capability. A field's own `owner` (see `FieldDocs`) overrides this for that field specifically.

protections.description: Documented safeguard: presence only, never an adequacy claim.

purpose.description: The declared reason this capability's data is collected or retained. Declared only: data-cap never verifies the stated purpose matches actual usage. A field's own `purpose` (see `FieldDocs`) overrides this for that field specifically.

retention.description: Documented retention policy: presence only, never an enforcement claim.

sensitivity.description: Data classification. Standard vocabulary: `"public"` / `"internal"` / `"confidential"` / `"restricted"` (ascending); custom values are allowed but flagged as non-standard, never blocking.

transferSafeguard.description: The declared safeguard relied on for any transfer of this capability's data out of `dataResidency`'s own jurisdiction(s): paired conceptually with `dataResidency`, same presence-only discipline. A field's own `transferSafeguard` (see `FieldDocs`) overrides this for that field specifically.

Loosen<EvidenceFieldDocs>.description: Every property here is always assigned (never conditionally omitted: see extractCapabilityDocs()/extractOperationDocsMap()/ extractEvidenceFieldsMap() below). Some are assigned an `undefined` value when the AST literal didn't declare it. exactOptionalPropertyTypes distinguishes "key absent" from "key present holding undefined". This type widens every property to explicitly include `| undefined` (rather than routing every assignment through a conditional-spread "omit if absent" instead). That matches what this type actually represents: a raw, unconstrained parse result, not a validated CapabilityDocs.

dynamicAccess.description: Citations of where this field is accessed in a way static analysis can't see on its own, such as a dynamic key derived at runtime. Each is `"<relative-path>:<line>:<column>"`. Every run re-verifies them. A citation whose file no longer exists, or whose cited line has visibly changed since it was written, is downgraded and flagged, never trusted forever.

Loosen<FieldDocs>.description: Every property here is always assigned (never conditionally omitted: see extractCapabilityDocs()/extractOperationDocsMap()/ extractEvidenceFieldsMap() below). Some are assigned an `undefined` value when the AST literal didn't declare it. exactOptionalPropertyTypes distinguishes "key absent" from "key present holding undefined". This type widens every property to explicitly include `| undefined` (rather than routing every assignment through a conditional-spread "omit if absent" instead). That matches what this type actually represents: a raw, unconstrained parse result, not a validated CapabilityDocs.

auditRequired.description: Whether access to this field is documented as requiring an audit trail. Declared only, same presence-only discipline as `protections`/ `retention`. Overrides the capability's own `auditRequired` for this field specifically.

dataResidency.description: The declared jurisdiction(s) this field's data is permitted or expected to be *stored* in. It is a policy constraint, not an observed fact, a processing-location claim or a data-subject-location claim. Overrides the capability's own `dataResidency` for this field specifically.

dataSubjectCategory.description: The declared category of data subject this field's data concerns (e.g. `"customers"`, `"employees"`, `"minors"`). Declared only: data-cap never verifies who a field's actual data subjects are. Field-level only, with no capability-level counterpart to override. Which data subjects a field concerns is a fact about that field's own data, not one a capability can state for every field.

deprecated.description: Whether this field is documented as deprecated. Presence-only, same discipline as every other declared fact here: nothing warns at runtime.

deprecatedReason.description: Why this field is deprecated, and what to use instead. Only meaningful alongside `deprecated`.

description.description: Why this field exists / what it's for.

expiresAt.description: When this field's data (or the credential/source behind it) is declared to stop being valid, as an ISO-8601 date (`"2026-12-31"`). Declared only: nothing expires anything at runtime, and `data-cap` never fetches a real expiry from a provider. Build tooling reads it to report what is expiring soon (see the Lifecycle Model). A date that has already passed is reported as expired, never acted on.

legalBasis.description: The declared legal basis asserted for processing this field (e.g. `"consent"`, `"contract"`, `"legitimate interest"`). Records that a basis was declared: never that data-cap has determined the basis is legally valid. Overrides the capability's own `legalBasis` for this field specifically.

metadata.description: Free-form extension bag for anything data-cap itself has no named concept for: opaque, never inspected or validated by any code path in this package. Once a concept matters enough for data-cap to reason about, it gets its own named field above; everything else stays here.

owner.description: Overrides the capability's own `owner` for this field specifically.

protections.description: Overrides the capability's own `protections` for this field specifically.

purpose.description: The declared reason this field's data is collected/retained. Declared only: data-cap never verifies the stated purpose matches actual usage. Overrides the capability's own `purpose` for this field specifically.

recipientCategories.description: The declared categories of recipient this field's data has been or will be disclosed to (e.g. `"payment processor"`, `"tax authority"`, `"internal support staff"`). Always explicitly authored: data-cap never infers a recipient category from its own dependency graph. A proven *consumer* inside this codebase is a different fact from a declared *external recipient*, and conflating them would misrepresent both. Field-level only, for the same reason as `dataSubjectCategory`. See `specs/decisions/0067-ropa-fields-recipient-categories-never-inferred.md` for the full reasoning on why this is never derived.

removeBy.description: The date by which a deprecated field is intended to be removed, ISO-8601. Field-level only: a removal deadline is about one field's own migration. A capability-wide `removeBy` would say nothing about which of its fields still need work.

renamedFrom.description: The previous name of this field, when it was renamed. Field-level only, for the same reason as `removeBy`. Build tooling uses it to read an added field and a removed field across two runs as one rename. Without it they are an unrelated addition and deletion (see `ChangeModel`'s `renamedFields`). Only ever populated from an *authored* value, never guessed from name similarity.

retention.description: Documented retention policy for this field: presence only, never an enforcement claim.

sensitivity.description: Overrides the capability's own `sensitivity` for this field specifically.

transferSafeguard.description: The declared safeguard relied on for any transfer of this field's data out of `dataResidency`'s jurisdictions, such as `"EU Standard Contractual Clauses"` or `"adequacy decision"`. `dataResidency` states where data may be *stored*; this states what protects a transfer *out of* that jurisdiction. Declared only: data-cap never verifies a transfer actually occurred or that the named safeguard is legally adequate. Overrides the capability's own `transferSafeguard` for this field specifically. See `specs/decisions/0067-ropa-fields-recipient-categories-never-inferred.md`.

Loosen<OperationDocs>.description: Every property here is always assigned (never conditionally omitted: see extractCapabilityDocs()/extractOperationDocsMap()/ extractEvidenceFieldsMap() below). Some are assigned an `undefined` value when the AST literal didn't declare it. exactOptionalPropertyTypes distinguishes "key absent" from "key present holding undefined". This type widens every property to explicitly include `| undefined` (rather than routing every assignment through a conditional-spread "omit if absent" instead). That matches what this type actually represents: a raw, unconstrained parse result, not a validated CapabilityDocs.

credentials.description: What's required to call this operation: descriptive only, never an authorization/enforcement claim.

endpoints.description: Declared data-flow boundaries this operation crosses: see `DataFlowEndpoint`.

metadata.description: Free-form extension bag for anything data-cap itself has no named concept for: opaque, never inspected or validated by any code path in this package. The index signature below stays so documenting never fights the type checker. `metadata` is the recommended place for new extension data.

response.description: Documented shape of what this operation returns/produces.

source.description: Short identifier for where this operation acquires/sends data (e.g. `"stripe-api"`, `"postgres:users"`), not prose.

ManifestCapabilityUpdate.description: One capability whose snapshot shape changed between two runs.

capability.description: The capability key (`file#exportName`) that changed.

changes.description: Human-readable description of each individual change (e.g. `"owner changed from... to..."`).

fields.description: The same field-level diff `changes` describes in prose, as data. It gives `ChangeModel`'s rename correlation a value to match, so no report has to parse structure back out of its own prose. `changes` is unaffected and still reads the same.

ManifestChangeReport.description: The diff between two `ManifestSnapshot`s, in a fixed Added/Removed/Updated shape.

addedCapabilities.description: Capability keys present in the new snapshot but not the previous one.

removedCapabilities.description: Capability keys present in the previous snapshot but not the new one.

updatedCapabilities.description: Capability keys present in both snapshots whose shape changed.

ManifestFieldDiff.description: The structured added/removed field-name diff for one changed capability.

added.description: Field names present now but not in the previous snapshot, sorted.

removed.description: Field names present in the previous snapshot but not now, sorted.

ManifestSnapshot.description: A persisted, JSON-serializable snapshot of the inventory at one point in time: see `buildManifestSnapshot`.

capabilities.description: Every capability, active or not, at snapshot time.

snapshotSchemaVersion.description: Bumped only on a breaking change to this snapshot's own shape. Bumped 1 -> 2: every capability key (`file#exportName`) is now built from a root-relative `file`, so a v1 snapshot's keys can never match a v2 run's.

ManifestSnapshotCapability.description: One capability's diffable shape at snapshot time: field/operation names only, never their runtime values.

active.description: Whether the capability was active at snapshot time.

citationSnapshots.description: Per-field citation integrity snapshots for declared `evidence.fields[key].dynamicAccess` entries, keyed by field name. Present only for a field with at least one citation that resolved to a real file at snapshot time (see `citation-verification.ts`).

exportName.description: The binding name the capability is exported as.

file.description: Root-relative POSIX path of the file declaring this capability: copied verbatim from `CapabilityNode.file` (see `display-path.ts`), which is what makes a committed snapshot diffable between two machines at all.

owner.description: Resolved owner at snapshot time, if any.

count.description: How many matching events were recorded.

field.description: Capability-qualified dotted field path: the Flow Model's field-node naming.

firstSeen.description: Earliest time any matching event carried (ISO 8601, UTC); absent when none carried one. Never used in the id.

lastSeen.description: Latest time any matching event carried; present exactly when `firstSeen` is.

scopes.description: Every distinct scope that contributed at least one observation, sorted.

scopeTimes.description: First/last seen per scope, ordered by scope; absent when no event carried a time.

skipped.description: Events (and skip reports) dropped as malformed: stated, never silent.

truncatedScopes.description: The scopes with a truncation, sorted: a claim built on one cannot be called verified near the cut. Absent when none.

truncations.description: What the recorder reported leaving out, ordered by scope, field, reason; absent when it reported nothing.

ObservationScopeTimes.description: First and last time anything was observed in one scope; only for scopes whose events carried times.

ObservationSkipReason.description: Why the walker did not record part of a value.

ObservationTruncation.description: Evidence the recorder knowingly left out in one scope: below `field` something was not captured. Names only.

count.description: How many times the recorder reported this (scope, field, reason).

field.description: Capability-qualified dotted path below which evidence is missing (the capability itself for the root).

OperationDocs.description:
Documentation metadata for one getter/mutator/subscription. Reserved keys are explicitly typed (mirroring the vocabulary real capabilities tend to document: what it does, where it talks to, what it costs to call). The type still accepts arbitrary extra keys for anything project-specific, so documenting never fights the type checker.

`credentials` is descriptive only: documenting `credentials: "user session"` is never proof that authorization is actually enforced. `endpoints` is likewise author-declared, never verified.

credentials.description: What's required to call this operation: descriptive only, never an authorization/enforcement claim.

endpoints.description: Declared data-flow boundaries this operation crosses: see `DataFlowEndpoint`.

metadata.description: Free-form extension bag for anything data-cap itself has no named concept for: opaque, never inspected or validated by any code path in this package. The index signature below stays so documenting never fights the type checker. `metadata` is the recommended place for new extension data.

response.description: Documented shape of what this operation returns/produces.

source.description: Short identifier for where this operation acquires/sends data (e.g. `"stripe-api"`, `"postgres:users"`), not prose.

OperationNode.description: One getter/mutator/subscription operation, resolved from the inventory's shared model.

docs.description: This operation's own declared documentation, if any.

endpoints.description: Hoisted from `docs.endpoints` for convenient lookup: author-declared, never statically verified.

hasOptimistic.description: Whether this operation's config object literal declares an `optimistic` key: structurally always `false` for a getter/subscription.

hasProcessor.description: Whether this operation's config object literal declares a `processor` key: a proven, structural presence fact (never an evaluation of what the processor does; see ADR 0050).

kind.description: Which kind of operation this is.

writes.description: Top-level field paths this operation's statically-extracted `writes` shape covers. Empty when `writes` was absent (on a getter/subscription) or unresolvable: never guessed at.

OwnershipCapabilityRef.description: Identifies one capability by where it's declared.

exportName.description: The binding name the capability is exported as.

file.description: Root-relative POSIX path of the file declaring this capability: carried through verbatim from `CapabilityNode.file` (see `display-path.ts`).

OwnershipFieldRef.description: Identifies one field, owned by a specific capability.

capability.description: The capability that owns this field.

field.description: The field's path within its capability.

OwnershipMatrixEntry.description: One owner's row in the ownership matrix: every capability and field they're accountable for.

capabilities.description: Capabilities this owner is accountable for at the capability level.

fields.description: Individual fields (on capabilities not wholly owned by this owner) they're accountable for.

owner.description: The owner's name, or `UNOWNED`.

OwnershipModel.description: `data-cap`'s Ownership Model: the owner -> {capabilities, fields} matrix, versioned for JSON publication.

ParseWarning.description: A recoverable issue found while statically parsing or linking one capability file: never fatal, always surfaced to the caller as data.

file.description: Absolute path (or synthetic label, e.g. `"(package) name"`) the warning applies to.

message.description: Human-readable explanation of what was skipped and why.

results.description: Every evaluation result, ordered by rule, subject, boundary.

rules.description: The declared rules, ordered by id.

PolicyOutcome.description: How a rule fared against one field (and, when relevant, one boundary).

basis.description: The weakest epistemic status of the edges the result rests on (`unknown` for an indeterminate result).

boundary.description: Id of the boundary node this result concerns; absent when none was reached or the result is about the trace as a whole.

edges.description: Ids of the edges on the path that justifies this result.

subject.description: Id of the field node the rule was evaluated for; absent only for `rule-matches-nothing`.

RenamedField.description: One added-field/removed-field pair correlated into a single rename via the current declaration's `renamedFrom`.

capability.description: The owning capability's key (`file#exportName`): a rename never crosses capabilities.

currentName.description: The field's name after the rename: matches an `added` entry in the same diff.

previousName.description: The field's name before the rename: matches a `removed` entry in that capability's own field diff.

ReportFinding.description: One reportable fact about the discovered capability graph. `severity` is assigned by the rule that produces the finding, following the two governing invariants in `AGENTS.md`. Static analysis never infers a relationship from insufficient evidence (an ambiguous case is `info` or `indeterminate`-flavored, never guessed at as `error`). A finding built from declared metadata (e.g. a missing `protections` field) never claims more than "documented" vs. "not documented."

capability.description: The capability this finding is about, if any.

exportName.description: The binding name the capability is exported as.

file.description: Absolute path of the file declaring the capability.

code.description: Which kind of fact this finding reports.

evidence.description: The records in the Evidence Model this finding rests on: flow nodes and edges, a policy result, an unknown (ADR 0070). Lets a reader drill from the finding to the analysis behind it, and lets SARIF show the path. Absent for findings derived from declared metadata alone.

family.description: Which analysis pass produced this finding: see `ReportFindingFamily`.

field.description: The field path this finding is about, if any.

indeterminateSites.description: Every candidate access site a `"FIELD_ACCESS_INDETERMINATE"` finding could actually be about: populated only for that code. Spans potentially multiple consuming files, so each entry carries its own `file` (`SourceLocation`, not only `SourcePosition`).

operation.description: The operation name this finding is about, if any.

position.description: Position of the declaration site (capability's own call, or field's own key) this finding is anchored to, when one is available: see ADR 0052. Additive: absent for findings with no single declaration-site anchor (e.g. a usage-scan finding whose subject is a consuming file, not a declaration).

severity.description: How strongly this finding should be treated.

source.description: The consuming file, for usage-scan-derived findings only.

ReportFindingCode.description: Every kind of fact a static rule or usage-scan/data-flow pass can report.

ReportFindingFamily.description:
Which analysis pass a finding came out of: an orthogonal axis to `severity` (how much it matters) and `code` (exactly what it is).

This is what makes the `--strict*` flags' own groupings legible in the output rather than only in the orchestrator's source: `--strict-docs` escalates `"governance"`/`"structural"`/`"citation"`, `--strict-ownership` escalates `"usage"`, `--strict-flow` escalates `"flow"`. With `family`, a consumer filters a report ("only what a usage scan proved") by one stable field, instead of a hand-kept list of `ReportFindingCode`s.

FieldDocs.description:
Documentation metadata for one field.

`owner`, `sensitivity`, `protections`, and `transferSafeguard` override the capability-level value of the same name for this field. Fields in one capability can differ in sensitivity, owner and transfer boundary. `protections` and `retention` only signal that documentation is present. A generator may say a safeguard or policy is "documented" or "not documented", never that it is adequate, correct or enforced. `purpose`, `legalBasis`, `dataResidency`, `transferSafeguard` and `auditRequired` follow the same presence-only rule. They are declared governance facts, never a claim that data-cap has determined they satisfy any law (see `specs/decisions/0051-documentdata-metadata-and-governance-fields.md`). `dataSubjectCategory` and `recipientCategories` are field-level only, with no capability-level counterpart; each property's own doc comment says why.

The boundary this interface draws is deliberate: a named property here is reserved for a concept data-cap itself understands, projects, or reports on. Anything else (organization-specific detail with no data-cap-defined meaning) belongs in `metadata`, never in an ad hoc extra property. That keeps this vocabulary bounded instead of accreting one-off keys over time.

Note what is deliberately absent: there is no per-field `validate`/ `validator` property, and no `helpers.validators` combinator library backing one, unlike `@maverickcer/env-cap`'s `EnvVarDocs`. That is a design choice, not a gap. `env-cap` validates on a reject-and-throw pipeline, where a failing validator must carry a message explaining the rejection. `data-cap` has no reject path to write a message for. Invalid processor/operation output resets the field to its declared default via `core/schema.ts`'s `checkValueAgainstSchema`. That keeps fields synchronously readable (`AGENTS.md` invariant 2) and surfaces the mismatch through `DataInfo`. See `helpers/shape.ts`'s own module comment for the full reasoning.

auditRequired.description: Whether access to this field is documented as requiring an audit trail. Declared only, same presence-only discipline as `protections`/ `retention`. Overrides the capability's own `auditRequired` for this field specifically.

dataResidency.description: The declared jurisdiction(s) this field's data is permitted or expected to be *stored* in. It is a policy constraint, not an observed fact, a processing-location claim or a data-subject-location claim. Overrides the capability's own `dataResidency` for this field specifically.

dataSubjectCategory.description: The declared category of data subject this field's data concerns (e.g. `"customers"`, `"employees"`, `"minors"`). Declared only: data-cap never verifies who a field's actual data subjects are. Field-level only, with no capability-level counterpart to override. Which data subjects a field concerns is a fact about that field's own data, not one a capability can state for every field.

deprecated.description: Whether this field is documented as deprecated. Presence-only, same discipline as every other declared fact here: nothing warns at runtime.

deprecatedReason.description: Why this field is deprecated, and what to use instead. Only meaningful alongside `deprecated`.

description.description: Why this field exists / what it's for.

expiresAt.description: When this field's data (or the credential/source behind it) is declared to stop being valid, as an ISO-8601 date (`"2026-12-31"`). Declared only: nothing expires anything at runtime, and `data-cap` never fetches a real expiry from a provider. Build tooling reads it to report what is expiring soon (see the Lifecycle Model). A date that has already passed is reported as expired, never acted on.

legalBasis.description: The declared legal basis asserted for processing this field (e.g. `"consent"`, `"contract"`, `"legitimate interest"`). Records that a basis was declared: never that data-cap has determined the basis is legally valid. Overrides the capability's own `legalBasis` for this field specifically.

protections.description: Overrides the capability's own `protections` for this field specifically.

DataFlowEndpoint.description: One declared data-flow boundary an operation crosses. A getter's or subscription's endpoints are typically `"input"`: where `execute` or `subscribe` acquires data from.
